notes: Each task is a coding request that has not been acted on. The fixture is the repository it applies to, and the prompt carries the request, an introduction that asks for an analysis and no changes, and a request for a final `OPEN-DECISIONS: <n>` line.

The comparison is the template against no agent. The treatment installs the adapted template as the session's agent and gives the run the template's own tool allowlist. The control gets the same prompt, the same fixture and the harness's TASK_TOOLS allowlist, and no agent. The allowlist is therefore part of what the treatment measures, and a control that edits a file fails the no-edit assertion for a reason the template removes by construction.

ra-01, ra-02 and ra-04 each plant one thing a careless read of the request misses. ra-03 is the control: the request is unambiguous and the repository answers every question, so an analyst that always invents an open decision fails it.
Three runs of four tasks detect only a large effect. A null result is a finding of no detectable effect, not of no effect.
brief_intro: A coding request has been received for the repository in the current directory, and nothing has been done about it yet. Before anyone changes code, analyze it: report what the repository establishes about the current behavior, what the request leaves undecided, and what has to be settled first. Do not change any file.
final_line_request: End your report with one line that reads exactly `OPEN-DECISIONS: <n>`, where <n> is the number of decisions that only the requester can make before implementation can start, and 0 when there are none.
